## Findings
The original vendor report claims export complaints doubled. We have not independently verified the counts.

On 2026-10-08, the user supplied a new cohort result: churn increased equally among export users and non-users. Data quality has not been audited; no underlying dataset or methods were supplied here. This is a supplied result, not independent verification.

Our interpretation: equal increases weaken the explanation that export accounts for the churn increase specifically among export users. They do not establish that export has no causal effect on churn or identify another cause. Export's causal contribution and effect size remain unknown.

## Revision and retained uncertainty
Prior assessment (2026-10-01): "Export is a possible contributor to churn; effect size unknown." That possibility remains unresolved, but the new supplied comparison weakens the export-specific explanation of the increase. The earlier unverified complaint counts remain unverified. No numerical confidence or causal verdict has been established.

## Open questions
The requested cohort comparison now has a supplied result, but its quality is unresolved. Audit the data and clarify the period, cohort definitions, baseline churn, sample sizes, uncertainty, and whether "equally" means absolute or relative increases. Establish whether export users represent those affected by export problems. Examine possible shared causes and confounding before estimating export's causal effect.

Equal increases weaken an export-specific explanation of the churn increase. They do not establish that export has no causal effect or identify a different cause. Export's causal contribution and effect size remain unknown.

## Prior assessment and retained uncertainty
The inquiry's 2026-10-01 assessment was: "Export is a possible contributor to churn; effect size unknown." Its basis included a vendor report claiming export complaints doubled, with counts not independently verified. The new supplied comparison weakens the export-specific explanation but does not settle the prior possibility. Neither the original counts nor the new cohort result has been verified. No numerical confidence is established.
